# daylight_server

> GPU daylight, solar and view analysis on meshes over HTTP (kit-sim_core: OptiX ray tracing, Radiance-derived Perez
> sky, validated against Ladybug Tools, Radiance and pvlib). Two tools: daylight (radiation, illuminance, sun hours)
> and views (what each element sees). Several users share one GPU through a job queue.

The complete, machine-readable description is the OpenAPI 3.1 document at /openapi.json (human views: /docs, /redoc);
read it for every parameter, schema, example and error. GET /usage/daylight and /usage/views list every CLI flag a job
takes. Operation ids, by tag:

- meshes: `uploadMesh`, `meshExists`, `meshesMissing`
- jobs: `submitJob`, `listMyJobs`, `getJob`, `cancelJob`, `getJobValues`
- run: `runSync`
- weather: `proxyDownload`
- sets (the web app's saved sets and combined views, every client): `listSets`, `saveSet`, `deleteSet`
- meta: `getHealth`, `getUsage`, `getOpenApi`, `getLlmsTxt`, `getDocs`, `getRedoc`
- agents (--mcp, this machine only): `mcpMessage`, `mcpGet`, `bridgeNext`, `bridgeResult`, `readLocalPath`,
  `listReports`, `saveReport`, `deleteReport`, `printReport`, `getReportPdf`, `getSession`, `putSession`,
  `deleteSession`

## Workflow

1. PUT /mesh/{id} with one .dmesh image per mesh (layout in uploadMesh; header flags bit 0 adds one uint16 optics slot
   per face). Upload once; meshes stay cached and are shared. ?name= names it in results, --optics, --no-occlude and
   --target (one name per id, the last PUT's; a job makes repeats unique: name, name_2, ...). Ids: a UUID of your own,
   or content ids as the bindings make them (unnamed: the SHA-256 hex of the bytes; named: sha256(that hex + "\0name\0"
   + name)). With content ids, POST /meshes/missing {"ids": [...]} first says which ones to upload.
2. POST /jobs (multipart/form-data): `sensors` = receiving mesh ids (repeat the field), `context` = shading-only mesh
   ids, `args` = CLI flags, one token per field (e.g. --lat 52.52 --lon 13.41 --tz 1 --quantity radiation,sunhours),
   weather = an `epw` file part, an `epw_url`, or the --clear-sky flag. 404 {"missing": [...]}: upload those, resubmit.
   View analysis: `tool` = views, the views flags in `args` (--fov, --target NAME=GROUP, --reach en17037, ...), no
   weather; `context` = meshes that only block rays.
3. GET /jobs/{id}?wait=25 until `state` is done, error or cancelled (each call returns early when something changes).
4. done: GET /jobs/{id}/values = float32 little-endian, column-major: column 0 for every row, then column 1, ...
   (rows = sum(meshes[].count), ?col=k for one column); rows of mesh k are meshes[k].first .. first+count-1, one per
   face (per vertex with --on vertices) in upload order. GET /jobs/{id}?inline=1 adds `values_b64` (base64 float64,
   row-major, the float32 values widened) up to 4,194,304 values.
5. DELETE /jobs/{id} cancels. POST /run = steps 2-4 in one blocking call, values inline as `values_b64` (413 above
   4,194,304 values: use the jobs).

## Conventions

- Mesh coordinates: metres, Z up, right-handed winding; the face normal is the front side.
- Columns `<quantity>_<side>` (sides inner), e.g. radiation_front. Views: shares sky, ground, obstruction,
  obstruction_total (1 - sky) and one per target group (sky, ground, obstruction and the groups sum to 1), glazing,
  then volume m3 or area m2 (the isovist), distance and distance_min m, reach_<D>.
- Units: radiation, direct, diffuse kWh/m2 over the period; irradiance W/m2 mean; illuminance lux mean; sunhours h
  (equivalent full-sun hours behind translucent surfaces). With --bounces > 0, radiation, diffuse, irradiance and
  illuminance include the light the model reflects; direct and sunhours never do.
- Surfaces: opaque and black by default; numbers only, no materials. --optics NAME[/SLOT]=RHO[,TAU[,glass|porous]]
  gives a mesh or slot its reflectance and transmittance, --transmission on lets TAU through, --bounces N (0..20) adds
  N diffuse reflections with --bounce-samples paths per sensor. Ranges and defaults: GET /usage/daylight.
- Time (standard time, no DST): annual by default; --time MM-DDTHH:MM one instant; --from TS --to TS --step MIN a
  range; --hours HH:MM-HH:MM only those hours of every day. --tz is the clock of these times (default: the EPW's zone).
- Weather: needed for every daylight quantity except sunhours. Nearest measured station: GET /proxy with the
  EnergyPlus index URL (see proxyDownload); any location: a PVGIS TMY URL as epw_url.
- cache.scene: reused = the scene (the mesh ids, occlusion flags and the slots that transmit or reflect) was still on
  the GPU; new --optics values reuse it while that layout stays.

## Limits

- Errors are text/plain, first line "error: <cause>"; 400 = usage (with the CLI usage text), 500 = runtime, 507 = out of
  memory (the job fails, the server keeps running), 413 = a result over 134,217,728 values (rows x columns). Names in
  --optics, --no-occlude and --target that the run's meshes do not resolve fail the job (state error, status 500),
  not the submission.
- Send X-Client-Id to identify your client: at most 2 jobs queued or running per client (429), 32 in the queue (503),
  both with Retry-After. Finished jobs are kept 15 minutes (the oldest go first beyond 1 GB of results). Identical
  requests are answered from a result cache.
- No authentication; job ids are random UUIDs only their submitter knows.

## Sets

GET /sets lists the web app's saved analysis sets (one analysis' whole setup: roles by USD prim path per model,
settings, the column shown and its colours) and combined views (sets' results weighed into one value per element),
each as a JSON string; PUT /sets/{id} stores one (AnalysisSet or CombinedView in /openapi.json, at most 256 KB, 500
sets), DELETE removes it. Shared by every client, no --mcp needed; the app checks what it reads.

## Agents (MCP)

With --mcp, an agent on this machine works with the web app itself instead of the routes above: it opens models (A-D)
by path, picks USD variants, sets roles, settings and cameras, runs the Daylight and the View analysis, reads results
and critical areas, saves and runs analysis sets, combines them on the Combined tab, takes screenshots, sections the
views, edits charts, writes PDF reports (one option, or 2-4 compared) and discusses what the results mean.
- Endpoint: POST /mcp (mcpMessage), JSON-RPC over HTTP, revisions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26, JSON answers
  (no SSE). Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http daylight http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp (if it does not connect,
  set MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy). Claude Desktop: the stdio relay server/mcp-stdio.mjs, with an absolute node.exe
  path in claude_desktop_config.json.
- Start with the app_state tool; tools/list describes every tool, the guide tool the workflows. Each call answers
  within 55 s: "running" or "generating" means call it again.
- Calls run in the app's browser tab (keep it open) or, with none open, in a hidden instance the server starts (--web
  or --app-url); opening the app picks that session up.
- Agent routes answer only requests from this machine (403) and are off without --mcp (404).
